                    WESTERN DISTRICT OF WASHINGTON

    IN RE VALVE ANTITRUST LITIGATION

                                      MINUTE ORDER

15       The following Minute Order is made by direction of the Court, the Honorable John C. 
16  Coughenour, United States District Judge:                                 
17       This matter comes before the Court on Defendant’s motion to seal (Dkt. No. 198) and the 
18  supporting declaration of Christopher Schenck (Dkt. No. 200). Those submissions categorize the 
19  information Defendant seeks to maintain under seal—including that contained within Plaintiffs’ 
20  motion for class certification (Dkt. No. 181) and the supporting declaration of Alicia Cobb (Dkt. 
21  No. 182)—into six categories. (See Dkt. No. 198 at 4.) Defendant then explains, in general terms, 
22  where each item falls and why it should remain under seal. (See Dkt. Nos. 198 at 9–15, 200 at 2–
23  44, 200-2 at 2–38, 200-5 at 2–8.)                                         
24       As will be explained in the Court’s anticipated order disposing of Defendant’s motion to 
25  seal, given the nature of the sealed material, which goes to the heart of Plaintiffs’ allegations and 
26  therefore the merits of this case, the Court finds that the compelling reasons (rather than the good 
1  cause) standard applies to Defendant’s motion. And given the volume of documents and 
2  information Defendant seeks to keep sealed, generic justifications for maintaining these items 
3  under seal do not meet this standard. See, e.g., Splunk Inc. v. Cribl, Inc., 2024 WL 582712, slip 
4  op. at 1 (N.D. Cal. 2024); U.S. Ethernet Innovations, LLC v. Acer, Inc., 2013 WL 4426507, slip 
5  op. at 2 (N.D. Cal. 2013). Perhaps predicting this, Defendant notes in its motion that it can 
6  provide the Court with a more detailed justification for maintaining each item at issue under seal, 
7  so long as Defendant is given leave to seal that rationale. (See Dkt. No. 198 at 3 n.1.) The Court 
8  will afford Defendant that opportunity.                                   
9       Accordingly, Defendant is DIRECTED to file a revised supporting declaration under 
10  seal (no corresponding motion to maintain this document under seal is required), providing the 
11  specific bases for sealing each entry at issue. (See Dkt. Nos. 200 at 6–41, 200-2 at 2–38,1 200-5 
12  at 28.) This submission need not yet address proposed redactions to the Schwartz Report (Dkt. 
13  No. 182-1), nor should it contain argument responding to Plaintiff’s contention that references to 
14  that report, contained within Plaintiffs’ motion for class certification, (see generally Dkt. No. 
15  181), need not be redacted.                                               
16       Defendant’s submission is due no later than May 10, 2024. It shall be filed under seal 
17  through the Court’s CM/ECF system and in native format (i.e., Microsoft Word or Excel) in the 
18  Court’s orders inbox. Separately, it should be served on Plaintiffs, who will have until May 24, 
19  2024, to file under seal a revised version of Appendix 1 to its opposition brief (Dkt. No. 221). 
20  Plaintiffs’ submission shall be filed and served in the same manner as Defendant’s submission. 
21        In light of this supplementation, should the parties wish to modify the case schedule, (see 
22  Dkt. No. 176), the Court is amenable to such modification, but only so long as the parties can 
23  agree on a revised schedule. If so, they may submit a stipulated motion to do so. 
24                                                                            
   1 In doing so, Defendant should review its submitted tables for accuracy. The Court has discovered some 
25                                                                            
   errors, as previously submitted. For example, Docket Number 200-2 at 7 includes a reference to Cobb 
   Exhibit 4. Defendant describes this as a third-party contract and/or a communication regarding such a 
26                                                                            
   contract. But Defendant described that exhibit, in Docket Number 200 at 7, as financial information.  
1                                                                            
2       DATED this 23rd day of April 2024.                                   
                                       Ravi Subramanian                      
3                                                                            
                                       Clerk of Court                        
4                                                                            
                                       s/Kathleen Albert

                                       Deputy Clerk
